notes.title: 실례합니다
notes.text: 실례합니다 ("I'm being rude") is how you politely enter a room, interrupt, or squeeze past someone. 실례지만… ("Excuse me, but…") softens a personal question.

notes.title: 수고했어요
notes.text: After work, Koreans say 수고했어요 / 수고하셨습니다 ("you worked hard") to each other. Leaving a shop, customers often say 수고하세요 to the staff.

notes.title: 잠깐만요
notes.text: 잠깐만요 ("just a moment") is one of the most useful words in Korean: to make someone wait, to squeeze through a crowd, or to stop a closing elevator.

notes.title: 안 or 못?
notes.text: 안 means you don't (by choice): 커피를 안 마셔요 (I don't drink coffee). 못 means you can't (not able): 커피를 못 마셔요 (I can't drink coffee). Using 못 politely softens a refusal.

notes.title: Phone manners
notes.text: Answer the phone with 여보세요. To end a call politely: 들어가세요 ("go on in" — a polite goodbye on the phone) or 끊을게요 ("I'll hang up").
